cues.en: UTF eight is perhaps the best
cues.zh: UTF-8 或许是史上最棒的

cues.en: hack, the best
cues.zh: Hack，也是能写在餐巾纸背面

cues.en: single thing that's used
cues.zh: 且被广泛应用的事物中最棒的一项，

cues.en: that can be written down on the back of a napkin, and that's how it was put together. It was... The the first draft of UTF eight was written on the back of a napkin in a diner,
cues.zh: 而它确实就是这么诞生的。UTF-8 的第一版草案就是在一家餐馆的餐巾纸背面写出来的，

cues.en: And it's just such an elegant hack that solves so many problems that I I absolutely love it.
cues.zh: 它是一个如此优雅的 Hack，解决了那么多难题，我简直爱死它了。

cues.en: Back in the nineteen sixties, we had teleprinters. We had simple devices that you type a key, and it sends some numbers, and the same letter comes out of the other side. But there needs to be a standard. So in the mid nineteen sixties, America, at least, settled on ASCII, which is the American standard code for information interchange.
cues.zh: 回到 20 世纪 60 年代，那时我们有电传打字机。这种设备很简单，按下一个键，发送一组数字，另一端就打出相同的字母。但这需要一个标准。所以在 60 年代中期，至少美国确立了 ASCII，即美国信息交换标准代码。

cues.en: And it's a a seven bit binary system. So each letter you type in gets converted into seven binary numbers and sent over the wire. Now that means you can have numbers from zero
cues.zh: 它是一个 7 位的二进制系统。你输入的每个字母都会转成 7 位二进制数通过线路传输。这就意味着数字范围是 0

cues.en: They sort of move the first 32 for control codes and less important stuff for writing, things like like go down a line or backspace.
cues.zh: 他们把前 32 个挪作控制码以及对文本不太重要的东西，比如换行或退格。

cues.en: And then they made the rest characters. They added some numbers and punctuation marks. They did a really clever thing, which is that they made a
cues.zh: 剩下的则用来表示字符。他们加入了数字和标点符号。他们还做了一件极其巧妙的事，就是把大写 A 设为

cues.en: which in binary
cues.zh: 在二进制中，

cues.en: binary one, two, four, eight, 16, 32, 64. In binary, 65 is one
zero
zero zero zero zero one,
cues.zh: 零零零零一，

cues.en: which means that b is 66, which means
cues.zh: 这意味着 B 是 66，也就是

cues.en: you've got two in binary just here. C
cues.zh: 这里末尾刚好是二进制的 2。C 是

cues.en: three in binary. So you can look at a seven bit binary character
cues.zh: 即二进制的 3。所以你只要看一个 7 位的二进制字符，

cues.en: and just knock off the first two digits and know what its position in the alphabet is. Even cleverer than that, they started lowercase
cues.zh: 直接砍掉前两位，就能知道它在字母表里的位置。比这更绝的是，他们把小写字母安排在

cues.en: 32 later,
cues.zh: 32 个位置之后，

cues.en: which means that lowercase a is ninety seven one one zero zero zero zero one. Anything that doesn't fit into that is probably a space, which conveniently will be all zeros,
cues.zh: 这意味着小写 a 是 97，即 1100001。不符合这个规律的，大概率就是空格（正好全为零），

cues.en: or some kind of punctuation mark. Brilliant, clever, wonderful, great way of doing things, and that became the standard at least in the English speaking world.
cues.zh: 或者是某种标点符号。精妙、绝伦、令人叹服的设计方式，它也因此成为了至少在英语世界的通用标准。

cues.en: As for the rest of the world, they... A few of them did versions of that, but you start getting into other alphabets,
cues.zh: 至于世界上其他地方，他们……其中少数人做过类似的版本，但接着就会接触到其他字母表，

cues.en: into into languages that don't really use alphabets at all. They all came up with their own encoding,
cues.zh: 接触到那些根本不用字母表的语言。它们都想出了自己的编码方式，

cues.en: which is fine,
cues.zh: 这倒也行，

cues.en: and then along come computers.
cues.zh: 然后计算机就出现了。

cues.en: And over time, things change. We move to eight bit computers. So we now have a whole extra number at the start
cues.zh: 随着时间推移，情况变了。我们转向了八位计算机。所以现在我们在开头多了一个数字

cues.en: just to confuse matters, which means we can go to 256.
cues.zh: 纯粹是为了把事情搞砸，这意味着我们可以用到 256。

cues.en: We can have twice as many characters.
cues.zh: 我们可以拥有双倍的字符。

cues.en: And, of course, everyone
cues.zh: 当然，每个人

cues.en: settled on the same standard for this because that would make perfect... No. None of them did. All the Nordic countries start putting Norwegian characters and Finnish characters in there.
cues.zh: 都为此确定了相同的标准，因为这样会非……不对。根本没有。所有北欧国家都开始把挪威语字符和芬兰语字符塞进去。

cues.en: Japan just doesn't use ASCII at all. Japan goes and creates its own multibyte encoding with more letters and more characters and more binary numbers going to each individual character.
cues.zh: 日本根本不用 ASCII。日本去创建了自己的多字节编码，包含更多字母、更多字符，以及对应每个单独字符的更多二进制数。

cues.en: All these things are massively incompatible.
cues.zh: 所有这些东西都严重不兼容。

cues.en: Japan actually has three or four different encodings,
cues.zh: 日本实际上有三四种不同的编码，

cues.en: all of which are completely incompatible with each other. So you send a a document from one old school Japanese computer to another. It will come out so garbled that there is even a word in Japanese for garbled characters,
cues.zh: 它们之间完全不兼容。所以你把一份文档从一台老式日本电脑发到另一台。出来的时候会变得面目全非，以至于日语里甚至专门有个词来形容乱码，

cues.en: which is... I'm probably mispronouncing this, but it's Mojibake. It's a bit of a nightmare, but it's it's not bad because how often does does someone in London have to send a document to a completely incompatible and unknown computer
cues.zh: 就是……我可能发音不准，但它叫 Mojibake（乱码）。这简直是个噩梦，不过也还好，因为伦敦的人得把文档发给日本另一家公司里

cues.en: at another company in Japan?
cues.zh: 一台完全不兼容且未知的计算机，这种事能有多少概率发生呢？

cues.en: In those days, it's rare. You printed off and you faxed it,
cues.zh: 那时候这很罕见。你得打印出来再传真过去，

cues.en: and then the the World Wide Web hit,
cues.zh: 后来万维网出现了，

cues.en: and we have a problem. Because suddenly, documents are being sent from all around the world all the time. So a thing is set up called the Unicode Consortium.
cues.zh: 问题就来了。因为突然间，全世界的文档时时刻刻都在传输。于是就成立了一个叫 Unicode Consortium 的组织。

cues.en: And in what I can only describe as a miracle,
cues.zh: 接下来发生的事我只能称之为奇迹，

cues.en: over the last couple of decades,
cues.zh: 在过去几十年里，

cues.en: they have hammered out a standard. Unicode now have a list of more than a 100,000
cues.zh: 他们敲定了一套标准。Unicode 现在有超过 10 万个

cues.en: characters
cues.zh: 字符

cues.en: that covers everything you could possibly want to write in any language. English alphabet, Cyrillic alphabet,
cues.zh: 覆盖了你能想到的任何语言的书写需求。英文字母表、西里尔字母表、

cues.en: Arabic alphabet,
cues.zh: 阿拉伯字母表、

cues.en: Japanese,
cues.zh: 日文、

cues.en: Chinese, and Korean characters.
cues.zh: 中文和韩文字符。

cues.en: What you have at the end is the Unicode Consortium assigning a 100,000 plus characters to a 100,000 numbers.
cues.zh: 最终的结果是 Unicode Consortium 把 10 万多个字符分配给了 10 万多个编号。

cues.en: They have not chosen binary digits. They've not chosen what that should be represented as. All they've said is that that that Arabic
cues.zh: 他们没选二进制位。也没规定该用什么来表示。他们只说了那个阿拉伯

cues.en: character there,
cues.zh: 字符，

cues.en: that is number 5,700
cues.zh: 编号是 5700

cues.en: something. And this this linguistic symbol here, that's 10,000 something. I have to simplify massively here because there are about, of course, five or six incompatible
cues.zh: 多。而这个语言符号，是 1 万多。我这里得大幅简化，因为当然有五六种互不兼容的

cues.en: ways to do this. But what the web has more or less settled on is something called UTF eight.
cues.zh: 实现方式。但万维网大体上定下来的是叫 UTF-8 的东西。

cues.en: There are a couple of problems with doing the obvious thing, which is saying, okay. We're going to a 100,000.
cues.zh: 做那个显而易见的方案会有几个问题，就是说，好吧，我们要到 10 万。

cues.en: That's gonna need... What?
cues.zh: 那需要……多少？

cues.en: To be safe, that's gonna need 32 binary digits to encode it. They encoded
cues.zh: 保险起见，那得用 32 个二进制位来编码。他们编码

cues.en: the English alphabet in exactly the same way as ASCII did. A is still 65.
cues.zh: 英文字母表的方式和 ASCII 完全一样。A 还是 65。

cues.en: So if you have just a string of English text and you're encoding it at 32 bits per character,
cues.zh: 所以如果你只有一串英文文本，并且按每个字符 32 位来编码，

cues.en: you're gonna have
cues.zh: 你就会得到

cues.en: about 20 something... 26...
cues.zh: 大概二十几个……26……

cues.en: Yeah. 26, 27 zeros

and then a few ones for every single character. That is incredibly wasteful. Suddenly, every English language text file takes four times the space on disk. So problem one, you have to get rid of all the zeros in English text.
cues.zh: 然后每个字符再来几个一。这太浪费了。突然之间，每个英文文本文件在磁盘上占用的空间都变成了四倍。所以问题一，你必须去掉英文文本里所有的零。

cues.en: Problem two, there are lots of old computer systems that interpret eight zeros in a row, a null, as this is the end of the string of characters.
cues.zh: 问题二，有很多老式计算机系统会把连续八个零（也就是 null）解释为字符流的结束。

cues.en: So if you ever send
cues.zh: 所以如果你发送了

cues.en: eight zeros in a row, they just stop listening. They assume that the string has ended there, and it gets cut off. So you can't have eight zeros in a row anywhere.
cues.zh: 连续八个零，它们就直接不听了。它们认为字符串到此结束，于是内容被截断。所以任何地方都不能出现连续八个零。

cues.en: K?
cues.zh: 明白吗？

cues.en: Problem number three, it has to be backwards compatible. You have to be able to take this Unicode text
cues.zh: 问题三，它必须向后兼容。你必须能把这串 Unicode 文本

cues.en: and chuck it into something that only understands basic ASCII and have it more or less work for English text.
cues.zh: 丢进只懂基本 ASCII 的东西里，还能让英文文本大致正常工作。

cues.en: UTF eight solves all these problems, and it's just a wonderful hack.
cues.zh: UTF-8 解决了所有这些问题，它就是个绝妙的 hack。

cues.en: It starts by just taking ASCII. If you have something under a 128
cues.zh: 它从直接采用 ASCII 开始。如果你有小于 128 的东西

cues.en: that can just be expressed as seven digits, you put down a zero, and then you put the same numbers that you would otherwise.
cues.zh: 能用七位数字表示，你就写下一个零，然后放上和原来一样的数字。

cues.en: So let's have
cues.zh: 那我们再来

cues.en: that a again. There we go. That's still a. That's still 65. That's still UTF eight valid, and that's still ASCII valid. Brilliant.
cues.zh: 那个 a。好了。还是 a。还是 65。仍然符合 UTF-8，也仍然符合 ASCII。太棒了。

cues.en: Okay. Now let's say we're going above that. Now you need something that's gonna work more or less for ASCII or at least not break things but still be understood. So what you do is you start by writing down one one zero.
cues.zh: 好了。现在假设我们要在此基础之上再进一步。现在你需要一种能差不多处理 ASCII、至少不会搞砸、而且还能被理解的东西。所以你要做的就是，先写下一个一零。

cues.en: This means this is the start of a new character, and this character is going to be two bytes long. Two ones, two bytes. A byte being eight characters. And you say in this one, we're gonna start it with one zero, which means this is a continuation. And then all these blank spaces of which you have five here and six here,
cues.zh: 这意味着这是一个新字符的开始，并且这个字符将会有两个字节长。两个1，两个字节。一个字节包含八个字符。而你在这一字节里，我们要以一零开头，这意味着这是一个延续字节。然后所有这些空白位——这里有五个，那里有六个——

cues.en: you fill in the other numbers.
cues.zh: 你把剩下的数字填进去。

cues.en: And then when you're calculating it, you just take off those headers, and it understands just these
cues.zh: 然后在计算的时候，你只需要去掉那些头部标识，它就能把剩下的这些

cues.en: as being whatever number that turns out to be. That's probably somewhere in this hundreds. That'll do you for the first 4,096.
cues.zh: 直接识别为计算出来的那个数字。那个数字大概在几百的范围内。这足够应付前 4,096 个字符了。

cues.en: What about above that? Well, above that, you go one one one zero, meaning there are three bytes in this. Three ones three bytes with two continuation bytes. So now you have one two three four,
cues.zh: 再往上怎么办呢？嗯，再往上，你就用三个1加一个0，意思是这里有三个字节。三个1代表三个字节，外加两个延续字节。所以现在你有 1 2 3 4，

cues.en: 16 spaces. You wanna go above that? You can. The specification goes all the way to one one one one one one o
cues.zh: 16 个空位。你想再往上？可以。这个规范一直支持到一一一一一一零

cues.en: x with
cues.zh: 后面带着

cues.en: this many continuation bytes after it. It's a neat hack that you can explain on the back of a napkin or a bit of paper. It's backwards compatible. It avoids waste. At no point will it ever, ever, ever send eight zeros in a row. And really, really crucially, the one that made this win over every other system is that you can move backwards and forwards
cues.zh: 这么多个延续字节。这是一个巧妙的把戏，你可以在一张餐巾纸或一张纸的背面把它讲清楚。它向后兼容。它避免了浪费。在任何情况下，它绝不会、绝不会、绝关连续发送八个零。而且非常、非常关键的是，让它在所有其他系统中胜出的原因在于，你可以前后移动

cues.en: really easily. You do not have to have an index of where the characters start. If you are halfway through a string and you wanna go back one character, you just look for the previous header, and that's it. And that works. And as of a few years ago, UTF eight beat out ASCII and everything else as for the first time the dominant
cues.zh: 非常轻松。你不需要字符起始位置的索引。如果你处于字符串的中间想往回退一个字符，你只需要找前一个头部标识就行了，就这么简单。而且确实管用。就在几年以前，UTF-8 击败了 ASCII 以及其他所有编码，首次成为了网络上占统治地位的

cues.en: character encoding on the web. We don't have that emoji bucket that that Japanese has. We have something that nearly works, and that is why it's the most beautiful hack that I can think of that is used around the world every second of every day.
cues.zh: 字符编码。我们没有日语那样的表情符号槽。我们拥有了一个几乎完美适用的方案，这就是为什么我认为它是全世界每时每刻都在使用的、最美妙的黑客技巧。
